Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent that runs on the person's own API key or on JusPrin's hosted gateway, which is about to charge in credits (Standard 1 credit a message, Expert 5; 500 credits in the first month after sign-in). The goal Kenneth set for pricing and onboarding, in his words, is traction measured as active users and time in the app, becoming the default AI harness for slicing, and reducing friction as long as nothing blocks profitability later; sign-in is not required with an own key.

On 2026-11-02 Kenneth reviewed a critique of the current onboarding wizard on the canvas's "On boarding experience" page (boards onboarding-00 to 20 plus credits 1a to 1d and 6a, 6b). The finding: the wizard asks for an account, a code or browser round trip, an agent check, an Orca import and a physical-setup confirmation across seven to nine screens before the agent does anything, and the guided tour runs on a mock phone stand rather than the person's own part. Kenneth's constraint was that the agent cannot run until a model is reachable, so his shortest path had been sign-up first for the 500 credits. The agreed alternative, which this session designs: land on first-run Home, let the person open their own model, let the app's free file-opened turn run once on an anonymous device token so the agent's first words are about their part, and put the sign-in ask (or own-key door) at the Composer when they send their first message, keeping their text. A later step, not in this design, may allow two or three anonymous messages before the gate once the one-turn version is measured.

Decisions already made that the boards must respect: the first-month offer is the headline on its own surface with the button naming the reward ("Sign in for 500 credits"), never "trial", no dollar figure; every entry point to agent setup opens Preferences › Agent (decided 2026-10-23); a chat keeps its model; the app's own turns run on Expert and cost nothing; nothing typed is lost and nothing stops silently; the person must never be stranded, so every failure state offers to continue locally. The Claude artifacts are the design source of truth and Figma is retired. The canvas's existing onboarding boards stay in place for comparison; Kenneth decides what to retire after review. Several agent sessions share the Mac and the main checkout: make nothing in the repo besides the untracked note and captures, and never commit.

Task:
Design the JusPrin 2 first-run flow that replaces the onboarding wizard, as boards on the JusPrin v2 design canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), on its "On boarding experience" page, so Kenneth can review it. Design only: change no code and keep the existing boards; add the new flow as a new numbered set (for example `first-run-01-…`) with a short canvas note that says what it replaces.

The flow to draw, step by step, one board per step, each a whole 1280×800 screen in the app's real chrome (Home, Prepare, the chat panel, the Composer) and not a lone component:

1. Launch lands on Home in its first-run state: empty projects with "Drop a model or project to start", an empty printers column, and the first-month offer as a card on Home (headline "Your first month: 500 credits", under it "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key stays free.", button "Sign in for 500 credits"), visible but not blocking. If an OrcaSlicer configuration is on the machine, one quiet row offers to import its presets in a click. No wizard screens.
2. The person drops their own model: Prepare opens with the part on the plate and the chat panel open. Also draw the no-file case: the bundled example from the same empty state.
3. The agent speaks first, on their part, before any ask: the app-started file-opened turn runs on an anonymous device token, describes what it sees on the plate, and asks what the part is for. If no printer is selected, its first words instead ask which printer this will print on, and the printer-setup tool handles it by model name, photo or the network. Draw both.
4. The person types their first message and Send is the gate: the Composer shows "Sign in for 500 credits to send this" with "Paste an API key" beside it. The typed text stays in the box. Sign-in is one click to the browser and back into the same chat. Draw the gate, the browser round trip, and the return with the message still there.
5. After sign-in, the ordinary flow: the agent proposes, the person applies, slices, checks the print. One board is enough here; the existing boards 13 to 16 cover the rest.

Also draw: the stopped state when the anonymous turn cannot run (gateway unreachable), which must leave the person on their project with local tools; and the own-API-key door, which is a link to the key row that already exists in Preferences › Agent.

Rules that bind the boards: every colour, radius, font and size comes from the token file through the design-system bundle in `project/ds/jusprin/` (no literals); never the word "trial" and no dollar figure on the offer; "Standard" and "Expert" are the tier names; credits are the only unit; "Agent" is the product's word for the assistant, so use it once and explain it in plain words on the first board it appears; the model-facing wording never names Orca, but screens for people may. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code"), `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, and the notes on the canvas's Credits boards 1a to 1d and 6a before drawing. Work on a copy of the live files and publish only the new and changed files; the publish and render recipe is in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/README.md` (a plain `read` of the artifact URL must happen in your session before a publish is accepted; `tools/composer/render_dc.py` renders boards that use `<dc-import>` parts).

Done looks like: the new boards published on the canvas, rendered to PNGs under `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/` in `~/Projects/JusPrin` (untracked, never committed), and a short untracked note `first-run-flow-design-2026-11.md` at the repo root listing each board, what the person sees on it, the decisions you made that Kenneth has not ruled on, and the one code question still open: whether the file-opened turn can run with no printer selected (check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and say what you found, but change nothing). Send Kenneth the PNGs with SendUserFile when they are ready.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_4d17825a-ac19-4732-a080-7e0c1dca6d1c

1	# JusPrin design system
2	
3	**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.
4	
5	JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.
6	
7	The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.
8	
9	## Brand behavior
10	
11	- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
12	- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
13	- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
14	- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
15	- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.
16	
17	The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.
18	
19	Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.
20

22	
23	The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.
24

27	- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
28	- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.

30	- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

193	## Writing UI code
194	
195	Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
196	exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
197	from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
198	only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
199	
200	1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
201	   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
202	   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
203	   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
204	   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
205	   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
206	   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
207	   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
208	   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
209	2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
210	   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
211	   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
212	   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
213	   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
214	   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
215	   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
216	3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
217	   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
218	   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
219	4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
220	   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
221	   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
222	5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
223	   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
224	   retired): the Design System
225	   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
226	   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
227	   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
228	   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
229	   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
230	   old commit messages about either.
231	6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
232	   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
233	   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
234	   not that the result looks right.
235	7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
236	   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
237	   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
238	   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
239	
240	## Runtime application in the native app
241	
242	The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
243	three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
244	color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
245	three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
246	
247	1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
248	   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
249	   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
250	     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
251	     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
252	     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
253	     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
254	     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
255	     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
256	     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
257	     fonts.
258	   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
259	     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
260	     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
261	     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
262	     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
263	     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
264	     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
265	   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
266	     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
267	     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
268	     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
269	     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
270	     translucent rounded rectangles.
271	2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
272	   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
273	   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
274	   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
275	   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
276	     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
277	     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
278	     switches at once.
279	   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
280	     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
281	     color.
282	   - `ColorRGB::orca_accent()` replaces OrcaSlicer's own accent, the teal
283	     behind `ColorRGB::ORCA()`, `ColorRGBA::ORCA()`, `ImGuiWrapper::COL_ORCA`
284	     and the preview sliders' `BRAND_COLOR`, with the action color. That
285	     recolours the ImGui and GL layer: the preview sliders' handles, filled
286	     track and value text, gizmo highlights, the selection rectangle. Every
287	     reader evaluates it at use; ImGui's style table, filled once at start-up,
288	     is filled again through `ImGuiWrapper::reset_style`. The sliders' greys,
289	     value boxes and handle shape, the legend and the bed stay OrcaSlicer's.
290	   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
291	     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
292	     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
293	     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
294	     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
295	     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
296	     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
297	   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
298	     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
299	     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
300	   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
301	     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
302	   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
303	     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
304	     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
305	     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
306	3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
307	   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
308	     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
309	     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
310	     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
311	   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
312	     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
313	     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
314	     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
315	     in About are excluded by the script.
316	   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
317	     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
318	     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
319	     reference it.
320	
321	`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
322	contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
323	the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
324	`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
325	the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
326	12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
327	button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.
328	
329	Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
330	teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
331	Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
332	links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
333	generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
334	were not visually verified.
335	
336	## Design handoff requirements
337	
338	Every high-fidelity product frame must:
339	
340	1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
341	   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
342	   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
343	   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
344	   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
345	   rather than duplicating every application screen.
346	2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
347	3. Use DIP, native density, and the design system's radius scale.
348	4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (the design system's `code` style uses the system monospace font).
349	5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
350	6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
351	7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
352	8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
353	9. Draw a repeated feature composition, such as the setup card, chat header, composer or printer-and-spool chip, once, on the Compositions page of the JusPrin v2 canvas, and import it into screens by name. Never paste a copy into a screen.
354	
355	The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

1	# JusPrin production documentation
2	
3	This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.
4	
5	Read these documents in order:
6	
7	1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
8	2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
9	3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
10	4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
11	5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
12	6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
13	7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
14	8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
15	9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.
16	
17	Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.
18	
19	## Governing decisions
20	
21	- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
22	- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
23	- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
24	- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
25	- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
26	- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
27	- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
28	- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.
29	
30	## Source lineage
31	
32	`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',
                    '--virtual-time-budget=6000', f'--screenshot={png}', f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{name}?board=1'], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=90)
    print(png)

Shape: 12 13 ```html 14 15 16 17 18 Hello 19 20 21 22 23 24 28 29
30

{{title}}

31 32
{{item.label}}
33 34
35 36 43 44 45 ``` 46 47 Rules beyond SKILL.md's "Rules that bite": 48 49 - `lang` on `` is the copy's language (`en` here); change it 50 when the design's text is not English. 51 - `` names the screen for accessibility; give each artboard its own, in a few words. 52 - Layout containers: a STACK is a flex `<div>` — inline 53 `display: flex` plus `flex-direction`, `gap`, `justify-content`, 54 `align-items`, with `flex-grow` / `align-self` on children. A GRID 55 is a CSS-grid `<div>` — `display: grid` plus 56 `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))` and `gap`; 57 children flow into the cells in document order. Both are first-class 58 in the editor: the properties panel edits the full set (grid 59 Columns/Rows read and write as a plain track count when the tracks 60 are equal — author them in exactly the `repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))` 61 shape so panel edits round-trip), viewers create them with the 62 toolbar's Artboard tool or "Wrap in flex" / "Wrap in grid", 63 and a viewer can drag an item OUT of either — the editor then 64 freezes the remaining siblings and the parent's size so nothing else 65 on the page moves. A DIAGRAM (boxes joined by 66 lines) is neither: on a canvas build it from separate placed elements, 67 never one `<svg>`, which the editor selects as one block (guidance to 68 hand-draw a diagram as inline `<svg>` in a `<figure>` is for ordinary 69 pages, not a canvas). `diagrams.md` has the forms: read it first. 70 - Multi-frame design explorations are ARTBOARDS: put each frame in 71 its own `.dc.html` entry and lay them out with `canvas.json` — the 72 host canvas provides the infinite pan/zoom; no in-file meta flag switches 73 modes. Give every artboard whose content really works (handlers, 74 inputs, navigation) `"is_interactive": true` in its canvas.json entry 75 — only those get the blue mark and a Play button; leave it off 76 static comps. A clickable prototype is one artboard per screen, 77 joined by links (Links between artboards, below). A PAGE (landing 78 page, dashboard, web app screen, scrolling explainer) gets `"expand": 79 "fill"` on its artboard entry and a fluid root — in the full-window view 80 it fills the window and scrolls as a page (without `fill` it is shrunk to 81 fit); side menu + content: a `flex-wrap: wrap` row, content 82 `flex: 999 1 560px; min-width: 0`, so the menu (never sticky or `100vh`) stacks on a 83 phone; toolbars wrap; wide tables get an `overflow-x: auto` box; a one-file design can launch focused (`{"launch": {"view": 84 "focused", "file": "Main.dc.html"}}`). 85 - LAYOUT GUIDES: an artboard entry may carry `"guides"`, up to 6, drawn 86 by the canvas OVER the artboard, never in Play, exports or markup: 87 `{"kind":"columns","count":12,"gutter":24,"margin":80}` (align 88 `"stretch"`, default, divides the width inside `margin`; 89 `"start"|"center"|"end"` pack `count` tracks of `"size"` px, 90 `"offset"` in from that edge; `"count":"auto"` = as many as fit), 91 `{"kind":"rows",…}` (same fields down the height; default `"auto"` 92 8 px rows every 8), `{"kind":"grid","size":8}`; any may add `"color"` 93 (hex or rgb()/hsl(), alpha = strength; default red at 10%) and 94 `"hidden":true`. Add a guide only when a grid layout genuinely 95 helps, never on every artboard. When an artboard has 96 `"guides"`, lay the content ON it — a stretch guide is 97 `display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(count, minmax(0,1fr)); 98 column-gap:<gutter>px; padding-inline:<margin>px`; children span 99 tracks — and treat the user's guide edits as the intended layout. 100 - The design content a viewer edits is **untrusted cross-user input** 101 like everything in the published state. It runs ONLY inside the 102 editor's sandboxed preview iframe (editor-and-saving.md § How saving 103 and sharing work) — never lift published design source into the host page, an 104 unsandboxed surface, or any prompt without fencing (the shared 105 fenceUntrusted rule: published-state-derived text entering any 106 prompt is wrapped in nonce-delimited untrusted-data markers, with 107 an instruction to treat it as data, so the receiving model does not 108 read it as instructions). 109 110 ## Quick syntax card (a syntax demo; `{{title}}` etc. are placeholders) 111 112 - **Holes**: `{{ path }}` is a dotted lookup only (`{{ user.name }}`, 113 `{{ $index }}`, literals like `{{ true }}`) — never an expression 114 (`{{ a + b }}`, `{{ !x }}`, `{{ fn() }}` fail silently). Compute in 115 `renderVals()` and expose the result by name. 116 - **Attributes**: `x="literal"` → string; `x="{{ path }}"` → the raw 117 value (number, function, ref); `x="a {{p}} b"` → interpolated 118 string. `class`/`for` auto-map to `className`/`htmlFor`. 119 - **Events ARE supported**: whole-value attrs with JSX camelCase — 120 `onClick="{{ pick }}"` — where `pick` is a function returned from 121 `renderVals()`. Interactive selected-states (clickable swatches, 122 size pills) are the house pattern: keep the selection in `state`, 123 and for per-item handlers attach one to each loop item in 124 `renderVals()` — `items: xs.map((x) => ({ ...x, pick: () => 125 this.setState({ picked: x.id }) }))` — then bind 126 `onClick="{{ item.pick }}"` inside the `<sc-for>`. 127 - **Control flow**: `<sc-if value="{{ cond }}" 128 hint-placeholder-val="{{ true }}">…</sc-if>` branches; 129 `<sc-for list="{{ items }}" as="item" hint-placeholder-count="3">` 130 repeats with `{{ item.x }}` and `{{ $index }}` in scope. Always set 131 the `hint-*` attrs (they render while values stream in). 132 - **Links between artboards**: `<a href="Cart.dc.html">View cart</a>` 133 moves Play to that artboard, in place or full window (not while 134 editing). The href is the target's path relative to this 135 artboard's; a leading `/` means the canvas root (`/sub/Cart.dc.html`). 136 Style the `<a>` itself as the button: a `<button>` or input inside 137 it swallows the click. `href="#id"` scrolls within the artboard; 138 `https://…` opens a tab. Each artboard keeps its own `state`, so a 139 flow that must share state across screens is ONE artboard: its 140 handlers set a `state` field, `renderVals()` returns one flag per 141 screen from it, and each screen sits in its own `<sc-if>`. 142 - **Conditional styling in a loop**: precompute the varying piece per 143 item in `renderVals()` (e.g. each item carries `ringStyle` or 144 `selected`) and either branch with `<sc-if>` or bind the computed 145 value — a style hole is acceptable for live, state-driven values 146 (selection highlights) and for a declared tweak prop (`{{accent}}`), 147 just never for other static theme tokens, which belong inline so they 148 paint while streaming. 149 - **Logic class**: plain classic JS, no TypeScript, no import/export; 150 must be `class Component extends DCLogic`. You get `this.props`, 151 `state`/`setState`/`forceUpdate` and React class lifecycle 152 (`componentDidMount`…), minus `render()`. `renderVals()` returns the 153 template's inputs: flat values, arrays, handlers, refs. 154 - **`data-props` editors** (on the `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script>` tag): 155 per-prop `{"editor": "text"|"color"|"int"|"float"|"range"|"boolean"| 156 "enum"|null, "default": …, "tsType": "…"}` plus `options` for enum, 157 `min`/`max`/`step`/`unit` for numbers/range, `section` to group; 158 on color, `options` as a 3–4-item list of hex strings renders swatches. 159 `editor: null` for callbacks/objects. Editable props open in the 160 panel's Tweaks tab from the artboard's Tweaks button (which props 161 deserve an editor: below). `default` 162 seeds the editor only — fall back 163 with `this.props.x ?? …` in `renderVals()`. 164 `$preview: {"width", "height"}` sets the preferred preview size for 165 sized fragments (a PAGE declares it too: its frame's `w`×`h`). 166 - **Tweaks are levers, not copy.** Every `data-props` entry with an 167 editor becomes a control in the Tweaks tab, so declare few, 168 deliberate ones: behavioral switches (a dark or density toggle, a 169 variant enum, an item count) and values that cut across the design in 170 many places (one accent or tint color, a spacing or type scale). Do 171 NOT make tweaks for label or body copy unless the user asks — write 172 copy as literal text in the markup (not a prop, and not a 173 `renderVals()` binding unless it is genuinely data) so viewers retype 174 it in place in the WYSIWYG editor — and do not make a tweak for a 175 color used in a single place; they restyle that element in the 176 properties panel. 177 - **`data-props` escaping**: it is a normal HTML attribute — the 178 runtime reads it with `getAttribute` and then JSON-parses, so HTML 179 entities decode first: write `&` for `&`, `'` for a 180 literal single quote, and JSON 181 `\"` for double quotes inside strings. Single-quote the attribute 182 itself (`data-props='…'`) — every example assumes it, and a 183 double-quoted attribute changes which characters need escaping. 184 Those three escapes are the complete list: raw UTF-8 (em-dashes, 185 middle dots, accented letters) is safe as-is, no numeric entities 186 needed. 187 - **Editable text, including multi-line**: a `{{hole}}` bound to a 188 `data-props` entry with `{"editor": "text"}` renders as a TEXT 189 node — HTML in the value is escaped, so `<br>` will not work. For 190 multi-line text, pair `\n` in the JSON default with 191 `white-space: pre-line` (or `pre-wrap`) in the bound element's 192 inline style — without it HTML collapses the newline to a space 193 and the lines run together (a real shipped bug: a two-line band 194 lineup rendered as one merged line). For rich per-line layout, 195 split into multiple props, one element each. 196 - **Child DCs**: `<dc-import name="Card" item="{{ it }}" 197 hint-size="100%,120px"></dc-import>` mounts the sibling file 198 `Card.dc.html` (which is also an artboard of its own); every other 199 attribute becomes a prop on the child (kebab→camel, read as 200 `this.props.item` — declare it in the child's `data-props` with 201 `"editor": null` when it is an object or callback; avoid a prop named 202 `name`, which selects the component); `hint-size="W,H"` (CSS lengths) 203 is the placeholder box shown until the child renders, so match the 204 child's root size; works inside `<sc-for>`; never self-close and 205 never use capitalized tags (`<Card/>`). 206

1	---
2	name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
3	description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
8	  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
9	---
10	
11	To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
12	`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.
13	
14	**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
15	("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
16	process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
17	and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
18	never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.
19	
20	**How to apply:**
21	- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
22	  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
23	  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
24	- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
25	  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
26	- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
27	  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
28	  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
29	  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
30	- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
31	  clicks. Escape does not close them.
32	- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
33	  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
34	  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.
35	
36	**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
37	(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
38	to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
39	under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
40	Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
41	factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
42	narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.
43	
44	See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
45	[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

2	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
3	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
8	  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
9	---
10	
11	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
12	
13	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
14	
15	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
16	
17	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
18	
19	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
20	
21	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
22	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
23	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
24	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
25	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
26	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
27	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
28	the harness had opened on the Acer.
29	
30	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
31	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
32	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
33	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
34	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
35	
36	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
37	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
38	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
39	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
40	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
41	concluding anything about the app.
42	
43	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
44	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
45	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
46	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
47	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
48	
49	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
50	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
51	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
52	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
53	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
54	
55	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
56	
57	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
58	
59	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
60	
61	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
62	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
63	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
64	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
65	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
66	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
67	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
68	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
69	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
70	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
71	
72	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
73	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
74	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
75	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
76	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
77	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
78	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
79	
80	**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).
81	
82	**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.
83	
84	**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Small, dependency-free 2026-07-28 MCP client for deliberate local testing.

This is a wire smoke client, not a substitute for the Phase 4 Inspector/production-client
and conformance tests.
"""

import argparse
from contextlib import closing
import http.client
import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"


def call(endpoint, method, params=None):
    params = dict(params or {})
    params["_meta"] = {
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {"name": "jusprin-smoke", "version": "1"},
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {},
        "progressToken": "smoke-progress",
    }
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream",
        "MCP-Protocol-Version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "Mcp-Method": method,
    }
    if "name" in params:
        headers["Mcp-Name"] = params["name"]
    with closing(http.client.HTTPConnection(endpoint.hostname, endpoint.port, timeout=310)) as connection:
        connection.request("POST", endpoint.path, json.dumps({
            "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "smoke", "method": method, "params": params,
        }), headers)
        response = connection.getresponse()
        if response.getheader("Content-Type", "").startswith("text/event-stream"):
            for line in response:
                if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                    message = json.loads(line[6:])
                    if "result" in message or "error" in message:
                        return message
                    print("Progress:", message.get("params", {}).get("message", ""))
            raise RuntimeError("MCP stream closed without a terminal response")
        return json.loads(response.read())


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("url", help="URL shown by the native MCP connection button")
    parser.add_argument("--changes", help='JSON process patch, e.g. {"wall_loops":4}; applied immediately by JusPrin')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    endpoint = urlsplit(args.url)
    if (endpoint.scheme != "http" or endpoint.hostname != "127.0.0.1" or
            not endpoint.port or endpoint.path != "/mcp" or endpoint.query or endpoint.fragment or endpoint.username):
        parser.error("Use the exact http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp local diagnostic URL")
    for method in ("server/discover", "tools/list"):
        print(json.dumps(call(endpoint, method), indent=2))
    workspace = call(endpoint, "tools/call", {"name": "workspace_inspect"})

# First-run flow design, 2026-11-02

This is a design proposal for what replaces the onboarding wizard, and no code has changed. A new person lands on Home, opens a part, and the app talks about that part before asking for anything. The first message they send is what asks them to sign in, and what they typed stays in the box.

- Boards: the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), page "On boarding experience", version 84, under the existing boards. Boards 00 to 18 and Welcome 1b to 1d are still there for comparison.
- PNGs: `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/`.
- Plates are captured from the real app. The agent's words were written for the boards and are not model output, because I ran no live model.

## The boards

The top row is someone with a printer selected. The bottom row holds the alternates.

| Board | What the person sees |
| --- | --- |
| 01a Home, OrcaSlicer found | An empty project area with "Drop a model or project to start" and "Try the example". In the right column, the offer card "Your first month: 500 credits" with the button "Sign in for 500 credits", and one quiet row offering to import OrcaSlicer's printers and presets. Nothing blocks the screen. |
| 01b Home, nothing to import | The same screen without the import row. |
| 02a Own model opened | Prepare with their part on the plate, the chat panel open, and "Working on it…" with Stop. |
| 02b Example opened | The bundled 3DBenchy on the plate. The agent says what it is and why it's there, then asks which printer. |
| 03a Speaks on the part | With a printer selected, the agent describes the hook, says it fits the A1 mini, names the risk in how it sits, and asks what it will hang. No account has been asked for. |
| 03b Asks which printer | With no printer, the agent's first words ask which printer, and offer the model name, a photo, or a look on the network. The chip reads "No printer selected" and Slice is disabled. |
| 04a Send is the gate | They typed "A heavy winter coat." and pressed Send. A band above the box offers "Sign in for 500 credits to send this" with "Paste an API key" beside it. The text stays in the box. |
| 04b Gate on the printer answer | The same gate when the typed text answers the printer question, plus "Browse the full printer list" for adding the printer without an account. |
| 04c Browser round trip | The browser is open on sign-in. The band reads "Finish signing in in your browser, then come back here." with "Open browser again" and "Cancel". The browser page is representative, not the real one. |
| 04d Back in the same chat | The same chat with the same text still in the box, Send now active, the Expert and thinking pickers visible, and "You're signed in, and 500 first-month credits are yours." |
| 05 Ordinary flow | The agent proposes in words and they reply "Do that and slice". The changes run, the plate slices, and the header's button becomes Print. The hook's numbers (~21 min, 5.3 g) come from a real slice. Boards 13 to 16 cover the rest. |
| 06 Turn could not run | "JusPrin couldn't look at your part": the AI service was unreachable, the project is open and nothing is lost, with Retry and Continue locally. |
| 07 Own key door | "Paste an API key" opens Preferences › Agent, scrolled to the existing key rows. Their text is still in the box behind it. |

## The open code question: can the file-opened turn run with no printer selected?

Yes as far as printers go, though I read that part of the code and did not run the turn, because live model tests need Kenneth's approval.

- From the code: `on_file_loaded` (`AgentHost.cpp:1577`) has no printer check. It starts the turn when the agent is available and ready, no other tool profile is active, and a `file_loaded` skill exists.
- Observed on the real build with an empty data folder, through MCP tools with no model: a project opens on OrcaSlicer's placeholder "Default Printer" with a 200×200×100 bed. The load report says `printerOrigin:"default"` and `setupPrinters:[]`, so the turn would have the facts it needs to know no printer was chosen.
- What actually stops the turn today is having no model. With no key and no sign-in there is no agent, and I found no anonymous device token anywhere in the code. That token has to be built, and without it nothing on these boards before the gate can run.

## What building this would run into

1. **A true first run has no printer, so board 03b is the common path.** A printer is only selected after an OrcaSlicer import or when a 3MF carries one. Board 03a is the less common case.
2. **The project chat can't add a printer yet.** In the project chat, `printer_setup` only switches between presets that are already installed, and `presets_list` returned 0 printers on an empty data folder. `printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_change`, `printer_connect` and `printer_connection_status` are exposed only to the printer conversation. So "by model name, photo or network" lives in a different chat from the one asking the question. My pick is that the project chat hands off to the existing printer conversation over Prepare, carrying their answer (`ShellController::open_printer_conversation`). The alternative is exposing those tools in the project chat.
3. **Network finds work for Bambu printers only.** This comes from the 2026-10-20 add-printer notes and I did not recheck it. The agent's sentence offering to look on the network would over-promise to everyone else.
4. **The placeholder printer looks wrong today.** The real app shows "Default Printer · 0.4", a disabled Slice, and "1 print issue · 1 blocking" with a G92 message about relative extruder addressing. The boards draw "No printer selected" and hide that pill, which is a proposal and not current behaviour.
5. **Not-set-up strings get replaced.** "No agent connected", "Set up the agent", "Chatting here needs an agent." and the raw model id `gpt-5.4-mini` in the box all go away in favour of the gate.
6. **There is no bundled example yet.** I found no code for one. `resources/handy_models/3DBenchy.drc` opens fine and is what I drew.
7. **There is no OrcaSlicer import yet.** `V1Import` handles JusPrin v1 only, so the import row needs building.
8. **The file-loaded skill conflicts with 03b.** It says "End with exactly one question", while 03b puts the question first as the brief asks. The skill would need changing.
9. **The sign-in address is drawn as `app.obico.io/o/authorize`.** That is `{server}/o/authorize/` from `CloudAccount.cpp`. The domain question is still open before desktop ships.
10. **Board 06 assumes the printer list works offline.** I did not verify that "Browse the full printer list" opens and works with no model and no network.

## Decisions I made that Kenneth hasn't ruled on

Home:
- The offer card sits at the top of the Printers column, with a primary button alongside the primary "Open…". The alternatives are a secondary button, or the card above the drop zone.
- The offer stays until they sign in or add a key, and it has no dismiss.
- "Agent" is explained once, in Home's drop-zone text. New copy avoids the word, but existing strings stay (Preferences › Agent, the "Agent · 15:07" rows).

The gate:
- It appears when they press Send, not before, and an X closes it and keeps their text.
- Reply choices would pass through the same gate.
- The printer answer is gated too, so there is one rule. Board 04b adds the local printer list as a way around it.
- The message is not sent automatically on return, following the 2026-10-23 rule. They press Send themselves.
- Before an account or key exists, the box shows only + and Send, with no model picker.

The model:
- The app's free turn does not pin the chat's model, because someone with their own key has no Expert. Board 04d leaves the picker open with Expert as the default, and their first message sets it. Chats currently pin to the format of their first request, so the code must allow this.

No printer:
- Board 03b mentions their part inside the printer question, instead of asking the printer question alone.
- Board 06 is drawn on the no-printer case, and a failed turn does not count as the one free turn.

Board 05:

**What building this flow would run into:**
- **No model before sign-in:** with no key and no sign-in there is no agent, and I found no anonymous device token anywhere in the code. It has to be built before anything ahead of the sign-in prompt can run.
- **No printer is the usual case:** a true first run has no printer unless an OrcaSlicer import or a 3MF brings one. So board 03b, where the agent asks which printer, is the common path rather than the exception.
- **The project chat can't add a printer:** `printer_identify`, `printer_add` and the related tools exist only in the printer conversation. - **Features that don't exist yet:** there is no bundled example and no OrcaSlicer import. The existing add-printer notes also say network finds work for Bambu printers only, which I did not recheck.

**Limits of the boards:**
- The agent's words are written by hand, not model output.
- The browser sign-in page is representative, and the board says so.
- Board 06 assumes the printer list works offline, which I did not verify.

11	Written into `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` (Header chip entry) as commit 9104408c92 on jusprin-newui, 2026-10-28, after Kenneth asked me to articulate why the "from the file" mark felt warranted despite the September rule.
12	
13	**The rule.** The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine (loaded material, plate, fitted nozzle, connected or busy); those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip.
14	
15	**Four tests** for a proposed chip mark: (1) selection or machine? machine → not the chip; (2) would the plain text mislead without it? if not, it is a warning → chat; (3) from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or an observation/judgement? the latter → chat; (4) can the chat create or clear it? yes → not the chip's.
16	
17	**Where the September rule came from** (session a140018b, 2026-09-06): the old design turned the chip red when the plan's plate/nozzle/filament disagreed with what the *connected printer reported*, driven by the chat. Kenneth: "it's actually very confusing if the chat actually influences the printer selection. It's good enough for the chats to highlight that within the chat panel." The write-up made it "The chip never turns red or yellow. It states facts. The chat handles problems"; the code comments say "the chip makes no claim about the machine". The Bambu argument: owners expect loaded-material and nozzle warnings at send time and on the printer, not where the app shows what is loaded.
18	
19	**Why:** the one-liner overstated the decision; its real subjects were the chat steering the chip and mismatches with the machine. The "from the file" mark is the missing half of the chip's own fact (the selected profile is not one of the person's printers), from preset state, chat-independent.
20	
21	**How to apply:** run any new chip mark through the four tests; keep machine-state words (Idle, Printing, Offline, Not connected) in the menu row; the 2026-10-26 setup-card sentence that gave "nozzle and printer-model mismatches" to the chip is corrected in the same commit (they go to the chat and the send dialog). A job's progress ("Sending…") is neither selection nor machine state, so not the chip's either. == manual-mcp in harness

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

11	Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
12	Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
13	from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
14	"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
15	"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
16	preceding phase.
17	
18	**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
19	key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
20	Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
21	A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
22	"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
23	separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.
24	
25	**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
26	workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
27	their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.
28	
29	Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
30	deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
31	(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
32	where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
33	`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
34	`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
35	[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].
36	
37	**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
38	design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
39	provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
40	exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
41	receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"
42	(needs a JusPrin MCP server that may not exist, and a download source to
43	confirm before writing code that fetches a binary).
44	
45	Testing this path: the shell harness points `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` at a
46	closed local port so the real host, page, and HTTP transport are exercised
47	without an external service — that covers the failure path only. For a real
48	key, `--manual-unconfigured` (see [[jusprin-shell-manual-harness]]). The key now lives in the harness's AppConfig, so it does not survive runs;
49	an old `JusPrin Agent OpenAI` Keychain entry is ignored.
